subject.title: fix(cron): detect ===DONE_ERR=== sentinel in agent final text as failure signal

question: Should `===DONE_ERR===` in agent-visible final text become an official protocol that controls persisted cron failure state and alerts, or must failures remain structured runtime signals only?
rationale: This is a durable behavior and compatibility choice: the patch changes the meaning of successful model output rather than repairing an established structured failure contract.

options.title: Keep failures structured
options.body: Reject visible-text classification and add or repair a structured failure producer at the runtime boundary if the reported cron run truly loses its failure signal.

options.title: Adopt an explicit sentinel protocol
options.body: Accept terminal sentinel parsing only with a documented producer/consumer contract, false-positive policy, and end-to-end proof of persisted status and alert delivery.

options.title: Pause this direction
options.body: Leave the linked report open for a narrower reproduction if no stable runtime source can emit a structured failure signal.

recommendation.title: Keep failures structured
recommendation.body: Reject visible-text classification and add or repair a structured failure producer at the runtime boundary if the reported cron run truly loses its failure signal.
